note: PARTIAL GT: 480x638 scan of a 19th-century French lithographed poster -- the hardest asset in the corpus (ornamental display type, shadowed/outlined letterforms, aged paper, mixed small-caps). Annotated 2026-07-31 by connected-component segmentation of each display line cropped separately (dark-on-light, threshold 110); the ornate letter-spacing splits words into several component groups, so 'BASTILLE' is reassembled from four groups spanning x84-330. Boxes are glyph extent plus ~4px, i.e. DETECTOR scale rather than tight: the recognizer needs that margin (a box tight to the glyphs of a comparable plaque word reads as garbage at 0.303), and IoU-0.5 matching is against detector-scale boxes. WORD level, not line level: an earlier line-level version of this file scored recall 0.0 because the detector emits word fragments here and a full-line box cannot reach IoU 0.5 against any of them -- that measured the annotation, not the detection. DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE: the '80bis AVENUE DE SUFFREN' / 'CHAMPS DE MARS' subtitles, the six-line programme block between y=500 and y=610, and the ~7px printer's credit at the foot are all unannotated -- readable to a human, but at 13-14px line height my box estimates carry +-3px error, large enough relative to those boxes that IoU-0.5 scoring would be noise. Being partial, detections there are neither credited nor penalised. Current failures this asset pins: 'LA BASTILLE' reads as 'IBas' at 0.392 over a box straddling the gap between 'LA' and 'BAS', and 'ET LA' reads as 'BT lA' at 0.387.
